description.narrative: Domestic resource mobilization (DRM) constitutes a critical fiscal strategy for the Government of the Philippines to usher in post-coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic economic recovery and sustainable financing of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The proposed program will help the government achieve its DRM plan by (i) enhancing DRM policies and legal frameworks, (ii) modernizing tax administration through digital transformation, and (iii) strengthening international tax cooperation and exchange of information. The program is anchored in the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023‒2028.2 A programmatic approach is adopted, with two subprograms during 2021‒2025. A programmatic approach enables the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to address the complex and challenging DRM issues systematically, building upon ADB's past engagement with the Philippines' tax reform since 2016 through project lending and technical assistance (TA) (figure). The program recognizes that DRM reforms necessitate not only raising revenue, but also designing a revenue system that fosters inclusiveness, encourages good governance, promotes investments and job creation, reduces inequality, and tackles climate change.

1.1. The government approved the 2022‒2028 Medium-Term Fiscal Framework which institutes domestic resource mobilization as a cornerstone national strategy to achieve the medium-term fiscal targets of public debt below 60% of GDP by 2025 and fiscal deficit below 3% of GDP by 2028. (DOF)

1.10. The government will implement carbon pricing mechanisms to reflect environmental costs of economic activities and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in accordance with the Nationally Determined Contribution Steering Committee on the Philippines' commitment to the Paris Agreement on Climate Change and establish the carbon pricing implementation framework. (DOF)
1.11. The government will implement enforcement mechanisms to ensure effective collection of taxes on single-use plastic bags. (DOF)

1.12. The government will roll out the Tax Information-Sharing System to foster seamless coordination of domestic resource mobilization between the national and local levels, which will enable the BIR and LGUs to exchange the necessary information of taxpayers engaged in businesses for cross-checking of revenue and sales information submitted to cities and municipalities for LGUs' assessment of local business taxes. (BLGF)

1.13. The government will implement digital payments for government collections and provide regulatory framework and mechanisms that will allow national government agencies and local government units to utilize gender-sensitive digital payment solutions to widen their digital payment network for revenue collection. (BLGF)

1.2. The government endorsed and submitted the House Bill on VAT on Digital Transactions to the Congress of the Philippines, which institutes the legal framework for the government to impose and collect VAT on nonresident digital service providers in the Philippines and remove ambiguities in the VAT system pertaining to the digital economy. (DOF)

1.3. The government endorsed and submitted the House Bill on the Ease of Paying Taxes to the Congress of the Philippines, which institutionalizes the Taxpayer Bill of Rights and streamlines tax compliance procedures and requirements for taxpayers, to reduce compliance costs for smaller taxpayers, especially small and medium-sized enterprises. (DOF)

1.4. The government endorsed and submitted the House Bill on Low Carbon Economy to the Congress of the Philippines, which: (i) establishes carbon pricing mechanisms for emission trading systems and other nonmarket measures for transition to low-carbon and climate-resilient economy; and (ii) mandates the DOF to be a leading coordinating agency on fiscal policies relevant to climate finance. (DOF)

1.5. The government endorsed and submitted the House Bill on Plastic Bags Tax to the Congress of the Philippines, which imposes excise tax on single-use plastic bags; allocates revenue collected from the excise tax for solid waste management plans of LGUs to protect the vulnerable groups such as the poor, women, elderly, and children from serious health hazards from waste; and encourages citizens to use environmentally friendly alternatives to plastic bags. (DOF)

1.6. The government adopted the competency framework for local treasurers to streamline business processes, service standards, and guidelines on local revenue collection and to strengthen local tax capacity and promote transparency of local tax administration. (BLGF)

1.7. The government approved the Executive Order No. 170 on adoption of digital payments for government collections, which mandates national government agencies and LGUs, with immediate effect, to provide digital modes of collecting payments for taxes, fees, and charges and to improve taxpayer services and efficiency of revenue collection across national and local levels. (BLGF)

1.8. The government will roll out dedicated systems that will allow digital service providers to register with the BIR, file their VAT returns, and pay their VAT liabilities electronically, to accelerate implementation of the Law on VAT on Digital Transactions and increase VAT collection from digital transactions. (DOF)

1.9. The government will establish and operationalize the Medium Taxpayers Office within the BIR to provide taxpayer services specifically for small and medium-sized enterprises, of whom, 55.8% are owned by women. (DOF)

2.1. The government will complete and implement all component modules of the Internal Revenue Integrated System which will serve as the BIR's central tool and repository platform for processing taxpayer information, to modernize and streamline tax administration systems and processes and improve gender-sensitive taxpayer services. (BIR)

2.2. The government rolled out the Online Registration and Updating System (ORUS) to modernize the taxpayer registration processes, promote voluntary tax compliance, and increase the number of registered taxpayers, which: (i) allows taxpayers to register and update their taxpayer registration data online; and (ii) accounts for specific needs of women, people with disabilities, and the vulnerable groups, who have limited access to internet and online tools. (BIR)

2.3. The government operationalized a Data Analytics Unit under the BIR's Office of the Commissioner, which conducts data management and analysis for use in tax administration and develop a data analytics framework that: (i) prioritizes the use of sex-differentiated taxpayer compliance and reporting data for tax administration design and strategy; (ii) identifies specific use cases for the BIR; and (iii) incorporates the application of data analytics outputs in BIR's audit selection framework, to create a robust data governance framework and promote the use of data analytics in the formulation and implementation of tax administration plans and strategies. (BIR)

2.4. The government rolled out BIR's electronic tax return system (eBIRForms) and Electronic Filing and Payment System (eFPS), which is used by taxpayers as online tax forms and the BIR for data upload, data entry, and return validation, to enable the government to capture and manage taxpayer compliance data and further encourage online filing and payment of taxes among the taxpayers. (BIR)

3.1. The government implemented a gender-responsive international tax competency program for BIR tax officials to strengthen tax audit functions, enhance gender equity in tax policy formulation, and increase revenue from taxpayers with cross-border transactions, taking into account specific training needs of female tax officials and ensuring equity in access to capacity development and career advancement. (BIR)

3.2. The government, with immediate effect, removed preferential tax incentives for regional operating headquarters and imposed a regular corporate income tax rate of 25% on them, on par with domestic companies and in accordance with the minimum standard against harmful tax practices under the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS, to reduce tax expenditure and address frictions in the tax system. (DOF)

3.3. The government signed the Bali Declaration and implemented the Asia Initiative of the Global Forum, an initiative on tax transparency for Asia to develop regional cooperation for tax transparency standards and better combat tax evasion and other illicit financial flows, to further promote tax transparency and regional tax cooperation. (DOF)

3.4. The government implemented the minimum standards of the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS for addressing international tax avoidance and enhancing tax certainty by issuing two regulations with immediate effect: (i) the Spontaneous Exchange of Taxpayer Specific Tax Ruling, which provides tax authorities with timely information on ruling granted to resident taxpayers; and (ii) the Mutual Agreement Procedure, which allows tax jurisdictions to resolve disputes arising from application of tax treaties. (DOF)

Action 1: The government will implement the e-invoicing system to improve taxpayer services through faster refund processes and enhance taxpayer monitoring, which will allow the taxpayers to electronically issue invoices or receipts and the BIR to incorporate the use of sex-disaggregated data for enhancing gender-sensitive taxpayer services and taxpayer compliance monitoring by gender. (BIR) Target date: 2025-06-30

Policy 2: Tax administration modernized through digital transformation Outcome 1: The Philippines received satisfactory rating and/or no recommendations from the Forum on Harmful Tax Practices in line with BEPS Action 5 Spontaneous Exchange of Information on Tax Rulings (2019 baseline: 3 recommendations) Source: Forum on Harmful Tax Practices Peer Review Report
Action 2: The government will implement the e-ORUS to enhance the functionalities of the ORUS and further improve taxpayer registration services, which will: (i) enable employers to register their employees with the BIR; (ii) implement digital Tax Identification Number cards for taxpayers; (iii) enable taxpayers to process secondary registration applications (e.g., authority to issue receipts, accreditation of computerized accounting system) online; (iv) and allow BIR satellite offices to provide taxpayer registration services to women, people with disabilities, and the vulnerable groups, who have limited internet access. (BIR) Target date: 2025-06-30
Action 3: The government will roll out the electronic one-time transaction (e-ONETT) system, which allows taxpayers to file real property transfer applications and documents online that is also integrated with the Land Registration Authority for streamlined processing of land title registration, to modernize capital gains tax collection from transfers of real property. (BIR) Target date: 2025-06-30
Action 4: The government will implement a single filing and payment platform for all taxpayers, which integrates the eBIRForms system and eFPS to simplify tax filing processes, encourage the electronic filing of returns, and increase tax compliance. (BIR) Target date: 2025-06-30
Action 1: The government will complete and implement all component modules of the Internal Revenue Integrated System which will serve as the BIR's central tool and repository platform for processing taxpayer information, to modernize and streamline tax administration systems and processes and improve gender-sensitive taxpayer services. (BIR) Target date: 2023-06-30

(DOF) Target date: 2025-06-30

(BIR) Target date: 2023-06-30

description.narrative:
Policy 3: International tax cooperation and exchange of information strengthened NA
Action 2: The government, with immediate effect, removed preferential tax incentives for regional operating headquarters and imposed a regular corporate income tax rate of 25% on them, on par with domestic companies and in accordance with the minimum standard against harmful tax practices under the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS, to reduce tax expenditure and address frictions in the tax system. (DOF) Target date: 2023-06-30
Action 3: The government signed the Bali Declaration and implemented the Asia Initiative of the Global Forum, an initiative on tax transparency for Asia to develop regional cooperation for tax transparency standards and better combat tax evasion and other illicit financial flows, to further promote tax transparency and regional tax cooperation. (DOF) Target date: 2023-06-30
Action 4: The government implemented the minimum standards of the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS for addressing international tax avoidance and enhancing tax certainty by issuing two regulations with immediate effect: (i) the Spontaneous Exchange of Taxpayer Specific Tax Ruling, which provides tax authorities with timely information on ruling granted to resident taxpayers; and (ii) the Mutual Agreement Procedure, which allows tax jurisdictions to resolve disputes arising from application of tax treaties. (DOF) Target date: 2023-06-30
Action 1: The government will adopt and implement international tax conventions to further expand the EOI networks with other jurisdictions to advance implementation of the AEOI standards to combat cross-border tax evasion and illicit financial flows. (DOF) Target date: 2025-06-30
